title: Energy cost and kinematics of level, uphill and downhill running: fatigue-induced changes after a mountain ultramarathon
authors: Vernillo G, Savoldelli A, Zignoli A, Skafidas S, Fornasiero A, La Torre A, Bortolan L, Pellegrini B, Schena F
population: 14 ultratrail runners tested before and after a mountain ultramarathon on level, +5% and -5% treadmill at 10 km/h
findings: Downhill energy cost rose 13.1% after the race (P < 0.001).
Level and uphill energy cost did not change.
Duty factor and stride frequency rose, and stride length, swing and cycle time fell, in all conditions.
Contact time rose and rate of force generation fell only on graded surfaces.
Performance time correlated with pre- to post-race changes in level (r = 0.52) and uphill (r = 0.50) cost.
limitations: Pre/post design with no control, 14 ultratrail runners, only 5% grades at a single speed (10 km/h). Positive correlations of performance time with level and uphill cost change were moderate (r about 0.5).
implications: Model a fatigue penalty on downhill cost late in long mountain events: +13.1% at -5% grade and 10 km/h after a mountain ultramarathon, with no change on level or +5% grade.

Include downhill-specific preparation in ultra plans because downhill economy was the only condition to degrade significantly; the abstract itself suggests incorporating downhill locomotion in training.

verification.notes: Crossref: J Sports Sci 33(19):1998-2005, 2015, title and journal match; Crossref lists nine authors (added Pellegrini B, Schena F to the author string). PubMed PMID 25751128 abstract supports all numbers. Removed unsupported 'race not standardised'.
